paper.title_en: Simulating the Hubbard model on a quantum computer as an advanced quantum mechanics project
paper.abstract_en: The Hubbard model is one of the most important models in condensed matter physics. It often is not studied in instruction, except possibly in advanced graduate courses. But, it is fairly easy to introduce the background needed to understand what the Hubbard model is and it is straightforward to create a quantum circuit that can prepare its ground state efficiently on a quantum computer for small systems. We show how to do this with a two-site model and focus on what is needed to be able to assign this as a project to students, starting from the fundamentals of second quantization to implementation on a quantum computer. This work proposes using a quantum computer in the same way as a classical computer is typically used in physics—to simulate a physical system—which is what Feynman had in mind when he first proposed the idea of quantum computing.
